bull.b: The $132 million PIPE and licensing proceeds improve near-term funding capacity and are expected to support operations and several clinical milestones through the second half of 2028. That runway can reduce immediate financing pressure while management advances the enlarged pipeline.

Adding multiple immune-therapy assets broadens Jasper beyond a single clinical opportunity and creates several development milestones, including Phase 2/3 work, a pre-BLA meeting, and first-in-human studies. A wider pipeline can improve the chance that one program reaches meaningful clinical or regulatory value.

Very low reported debt limits near-term refinancing and solvency pressure, an advantage for a company funding clinical development. This leaves more financial flexibility to direct available capital toward research and trials, although it does not offset the company’s operating losses.

bear.b: Jasper has no reported revenue and continues to post substantial losses, with a TTM net loss of about $31.8 million. Without commercial sales, the business lacks operating revenue to absorb R&D costs, so profitability remains dependent on successful development and approval of its candidates.

Operating and free cash flow remain deeply negative, including TTM operating cash flow of about negative $60.3 million. Persistent cash consumption makes the company reliant on new capital or other funding and can force difficult prioritization as clinical development continues.

The financing and acquisition materially dilute legacy holders: former Jasper holders are expected to own about 6.68% of the enlarged company, while total common shares rise to about 653.6 million. This reduces existing holders’ proportional participation and makes future value creation dependent on the combined pipeline.
